t: Goguryeo grew from a clan federation on the Yalu into the largest of Korea's Three Kingdoms, ruling Manchuria and the northern peninsula.
It took the Chinese commandery of Lelang in 313 and adopted Buddhism, a Confucian academy and a law code under King Sosurim.
Its fortresses held off Sui and Tang invasions for seventy years before a Tang and Silla alliance took Pyongyang in 668.
dyk: Goguryeo itself was often called Goryeo from the 5th century, and through the later kingdom of Goryeo that name became the English word Korea.
ev: Traditional founding of Goguryeo by Jumong at Jolbon
Goguryeo captures the Lelang commandery, ending Chinese rule around Pyongyang
Buddhism is received and the Taehak academy founded under King Sosurim
King Jangsu erects the stele of Gwanggaeto the Great at Ji'an
The capital moves from Gungnae to Pyongyang
Jangsu takes the Baekje capital Hanseong
Eulji Mundeok routs a Sui army at the Salsu River
Tang and Silla forces take Pyongyang; the kingdom ends

f.capital: Jolbon; Gungnae (Ji'an) from c. 3 CE; Pyongyang from 427
